nodes.description: Germline Nrros-deficient mice develop motor defects and die before 6 months of age; normal microglia are absent and perivascular macrophage-like myeloid cells populate the CNS.

CD68-positive, MHC class II-positive foamy macrophages accumulate, mostly around vessels, throughout the cerebral and cerebellar white matter and the descending corticospinal tracts. In Nrros-deficient mice, perivascular macrophage-like myeloid cells take the place of normal microglia. The foamy cells are p22phox-positive, which is relevant to the separate NRROS role as a negative regulator of NOX2.
